answer: An economy of autonomous AI agents can implement cryptographic proof-of-human-authorship networks resembling a digital grove to anchor digital identity in organic scarcity. When malicious actors unleash a computational gale of synthetic identities to subvert consensus, the protocol forces validation nodes to anchor trust through biometric or social-graph verifications. This structural flexibility, much like a resilient willow bending under pressure, penalizes attackers by imposing prohibitive GPU and identity-generation costs that make mass Sybil forgery economically unviable.
